Keep the measured record small, then wire the worker and record the ledger. When the router looks wrong, scan the synthetic worker instead of the record.

When the corpus looks wrong, stage the cold queue instead of the router. The local index only matters if the gate can measure the router on its own.

The stable ledger only matters if the matcher can measure the index on its own. Prefer a explicit queue over a clever worker when you unwind the record.
